Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Acme - procurement path and PO exception follow-up

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can line up next steps with procurement: 

- Quick recap: You and Tom are evaluating Redwood for inference serving for your ML platform (starting with the recommendations engine). We covered hosted API vs Dedicated capacity and the expected monthly spend profile (~$40k–$70k/month in year 1 depending on rollout).
- Procurement question: Can Acme accept a standard PO for Redwood invoices, or do you require payment by corporate card / prepay?
- Marketplace: Any preference for purchasing via AWS Marketplace (striped billing) vs direct Redwood contract?
- Timing: What's the procurement lead time (SOW + PO) we should plan for?

If a PO is required, any specific invoice contact and billing address we should use? If a PO is not possible, can we discuss an exception (prepay, upfront invoice, or marketplace route)?

I can loop in our finance/GC to document any exception path — want to avoid surprises on the pricing side.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123


From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmecorp.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - procurement path and PO exception follow-up

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the summary. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- We do not allow traditional vendor POs for SaaS subscriptions unless the vendor is listed on our vendor master with an approved payment profile. For new vendors, procurement typically requires payment by corporate card or prepayment via wire.
- AWS Marketplace is preferred if available because it goes through our cloud procurement and is easier for subscription management. Does Redwood have a marketplace listing?
- We may be able to make an exception for PO if the spend exceeds our threshold and we can get Legal to sign a master agreement, but that process is slow.

Our constraints: the procurement team will not issue a PO without vendor setup, and vendor setup requires a W-9 + bank details + a signed MSA for amounts > $50k/month. If Redwood needs a PO-based path, we would need to accelerate vendor onboarding with our vendor ops team.

Happy to connect procurement/finance if that helps.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Director, Vendor Ops | Acme Corp
S: samantha.lee@acmecorp.com

Thanks for the context, Ben.

We have a few practical routes here — call out pros/cons and what we need from Acme to move quickly: 

1) AWS Marketplace (preferred if available)
   - Pros: Faster procurement for Acme, consolidated billing, lower vendor onboarding friction.
   - Cons: Needs Redwood listing for the product/plan they want; takes ~2–3 weeks to provision SKU + entitlements.

2) Short-term prepay (quarter upfront) invoiced to Acme
   - Pros: Fast (can be issued same week), avoids vendor master setup for short term.
   - Cons: Revenue recognition/finance approvals required; Acme must agree to prepay on wire or card.

3) PO exception + MSA (longer path)
   - Pros: Long-term stable; allows standard PO billing.
   - Cons: Requires signed MSA + vendor onboarding; ~4–8 weeks typical.

What we need from Acme to proceed: billing contact + tax (W-9) and confirmation of acceptable payment method for prepay (wire vs card). If they prefer marketplace, we need to confirm the exact product/seat SKU they want and whether their finance team will accept marketplace procurement.

I attached a short procurement-exception-form to capture vendor onboarding fields and a draft SOW (SOW-draft.docx) to speed MSA discussions.

If Acme can do a quarter prepay for Q2 while we complete vendor onboarding / marketplace SKU provisioning, we can keep the project timeline intact.

Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Attachments: procurement-exception-form.pdf, SOW-draft.docx

Ben / Marissa —

We can support a few short-term options: 

- 30/90 day prepay invoice (wire or card) — Finance will need a PO# or internal reference for reconciliation but can accept card payments for new customers.
- P-Card (Procurement card) set up: if Acme's finance can submit a P-Card payment, that usually bypasses vendor master.
- We can fast-track an MSA signature for >$50k/month cases; Legal will prioritize but still needs the draft SOW and company legal entity details.

If Acme can confirm billing contact and whether they prefer wire vs card, we'll prepare the Q2 invoice and the procurement-exception-form to collect vendor onboarding docs.

Proposed next step: Ben, can you ask Samantha to confirm the billing contact and whether Acme will accept a quarter prepay on card? If yes, Marissa will prepare the invoice and I will include standard prepay terms.
